definition_zh: 苹果；苹果树；掌上明珠；喉结；纽约市
definition_en: the round fruit of a tree of the rose family; also the tree itself, and several idioms built on the fruit
core_image: 掌心一颗圆果子，红皮上还挂着果园的露水
scene: 清晨的果园里，竹篮中新摘的果子还带着露水。She polished an apple on her sleeve before taking a bite.
sceneCN: 这里 apple 是「苹果果实」（第 1 个义项：苹果树所结的圆形果实）；句意为「她在袖子上把苹果擦亮，然后咬了一口」。画面里有竹篮、带露水的果实和成排的果树。

pos.zh: 名词：苹果；苹果树；掌上明珠；喉结；纽约市

derivatives.zh: 由 apple 与 jack 复合，义为「苹果白兰地」
由 apple 与 wood 复合，义为「苹果木」
由 crab 与 apple 复合，义为「山楂果；野苹果」
由 pine 与 apple 复合，义为「菠萝」，早期因形似苹果而得名

senses.title: The fruit
senses.definition: the round fruit with red, green, or yellow skin and firm flesh that grows on a tree of the rose family
senses.definitionCN: 苹果树所结的圆形果实，表皮呈红、绿或黄色，果肉坚实
senses.example: She cut the apple into four pieces and shared them.
senses.exampleCN: 她把苹果切成四块分给大家。
senses.why: Old English æppel named this fruit first, and the fruit has stayed at the centre of the word ever since.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 æppel 最先命名的就是这枚果实，此后果实一直是这个词的中心。

senses.title: The tree that bears it
senses.definition: the tree that produces apples, widely grown in orchards of the temperate zone
senses.definitionCN: 结出苹果的树，广泛种植于温带的果园
senses.example: The old apple still gives fruit every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 那棵老苹果树每年秋天仍结果。
senses.why: Because the fruit and the tree that bears it were named by one word, the bearer can stand under the same name as what it bears.
senses.whyCN: 因为果实与结出果实的树共用同一个词，结出果实的一方可以与果实同名。

senses.title: A person cherished above others
senses.definition: in the apple of one's eye, a person or thing loved more than any other
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the apple of one's eye，指被爱得胜过一切的人或物
senses.example: His youngest daughter was the apple of his eye.
senses.exampleCN: 他的小女儿是他的掌上明珠。
senses.why: The pupil of the eye was once called the apple because it is round; to keep someone in that spot is to keep them at the very centre of sight and love.
senses.whyCN: 瞳孔曾因圆润而被称作苹果；把某人放在那个位置上，就是把他放在视线与爱的最中心。

senses.title: The lump in the throat
senses.definition: in Adam's apple, the cartilage ridge at the front of the neck, more prominent in men
senses.definitionCN: 用于 Adam's apple，指颈前由软骨形成的突起，男性更为明显
senses.example: His Adam's apple moved as he swallowed the cold water.
senses.exampleCN: 他咽下那口凉水时，喉结动了一下。
senses.why: The name joins the first man of Genesis to the fruit he is said to have eaten; the lump was imagined as that fruit stuck in the throat.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字把《创世记》里的第一个人与他据说吃下的果子连在一起，喉部的突起被想象成卡在喉咙里的那枚果子。

senses.title: A nickname for New York
senses.definition: in the Big Apple, an informal name for New York City
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the Big Apple，指纽约市的非正式名称
senses.example: She moved to the Big Apple to study music.
senses.exampleCN: 她搬到纽约去学音乐。
senses.why: The nickname is often traced to jazz musicians of the 1920s, who called the city the big apple; its exact origin is disputed.
senses.whyCN: 这个绰号常被追溯到二十世纪二十年代的爵士乐手，他们把这城市称作大苹果；确切来源仍有争议。

intro.en: Apple is a native Germanic word, and the whole family gathers around one round fruit.
intro.cn: apple 是本土的日耳曼词，整族词都围绕一颗圆果聚集。

items.en: The fruit word is reconstructed as 「*h₂ébōl」 or 「*ab(e)l-」, a stem shared by several branches of the family. The exact reconstruction and its spread are source uncertain.
items.cn: 这个果实词被重构为「*h₂ébōl」或「*ab(e)l-」，语系中多个分支共享这个词干。确切的重构形式与传播路径来源存疑。

items.en: 「*apluz」 is the reconstructed Germanic form, with Old Norse epli and Old High German apful as close relatives.
items.cn: 「*apluz」是重构的原始日耳曼语形式，古诺尔斯语 epli 与古高地德语 apful 是它的近亲。

items.en: Æppel is recorded in Old English for the fruit and, more broadly, for fruit in general.
items.cn: 古英语用 æppel 指这种果实，也较宽泛地指一般水果。

items.en: Appel survives into Middle English; the general sense of fruit recedes and the apple proper takes over.
items.cn: appel 进入中古英语；「水果」的泛义退去，苹果本身的意思占了主导。

items.en: The fruit gives the language a cluster of idioms: the apple of one's eye, Adam's apple and the Big Apple.
items.cn: 这枚果实为英语留下了一串习语：掌上明珠、喉结与大苹果。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that resemble apple in spelling or sound; the near-meaning group gathers fruit words and orchard terms.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写或读音与 apple 相近的词；近义组收水果与果园相关的词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to shock or dismay; spelled appall in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使震惊、使惊骇」，美式拼作 appall。

entries.definition: Clothing, especially of a formal or ceremonial kind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「衣服」，尤指正式或礼仪性的服装。

entries.definition: A request for help or sympathy, or the quality of attracting interest.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「呼吁、恳求」或「吸引力」。

entries.definition: The general word for the seed-bearing part of a plant.
entries.definitionCN: 植物带种子部分的通称，即「水果」的上位词。

entries.definition: A fruit such as an apple or pear, with a core and a fleshy outer layer.
entries.definitionCN: 苹果、梨一类有果心与肉质外层的果实，即「梨果」。

entries.definition: A piece of land planted with fruit trees.
entries.definitionCN: 种植果树的园地，即「果园」。

entries.definition: A drink made by fermenting apple juice.
entries.definitionCN: 由苹果汁发酵制成的饮品，即「苹果酒」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from the fruit to its tree, its idioms and its city nickname.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从果实走到果树、习语与城市绰号。

normal.en: The fruit is first: a round apple in the hand.
normal.cn: 先记果实：手里一颗圆苹果。

normal.en: The tree borrows the name: an apple tree bears apples.
normal.cn: 果树借名：苹果树结苹果。

normal.en: The pupil was once called the apple, hence the apple of one's eye.
normal.cn: 瞳孔曾被称作苹果，于是有了掌上明珠。

normal.en: Adam's apple is the fruit imagined stuck in the throat.
normal.cn: 喉结是把果子想象成卡在喉咙里。

normal.en: The Big Apple is New York, a nickname from jazz.
normal.cn: 大苹果就是纽约，这个绰号来自爵士乐。

abstract.en: One round shape travels from fruit to eye to throat.
abstract.cn: 一个圆形从果实走到眼睛，再走到喉咙。

abstract.en: The same word can be food, tree, loved one, body part and city.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以是食物、树、所爱的人、身体部位与城市。

abstract.en: The word shows how concrete things turn into idioms.
abstract.cn: 这个词展示了具体事物如何变成习语。

examples.en: She polished an apple on her sleeve before taking a bite.
examples.cn: 她在袖子上把苹果擦亮，然后咬了一口。

examples.en: The old apple still gives fruit every autumn.
examples.cn: 那棵老苹果树每年秋天仍结果。

examples.en: His youngest daughter was the apple of his eye.
examples.cn: 他的小女儿是他的掌上明珠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆」——阿婆从篮子里拿出一个红苹果递给你：苹果

root: apple 来自古英语 æppel，源头可追到原始日耳曼语的重构形式，再往上是原始印欧语的果实词，确切形式存疑。古英语时期它既指苹果，也泛指水果；中古英语 appel 之后，「水果」的泛义退去，苹果本身成为主义。现代英语里，这枚果实又长出一串习语：瞳孔因圆润得名，于是有掌上明珠；喉结被想象成卡住的果子，于是有喉结一称；爵士乐手把纽约叫作大苹果。

sensesIntro.en: Five uses grow out of one round fruit: the fruit itself, the tree that bears it, a cherished person, the lump in the throat, and a nickname for a city.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个用法从一颗圆果长出来：果实本身、结出果实的树、被珍爱的人、喉部的突起，以及一座城市的绰号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round fruit held in the palm, its skin still wet with orchard dew.
core.cn: 核心意象：掌心托着一颗圆果，果皮上还带着果园的露水。

branches.en: THE FRUIT LINE: the round fruit is the centre of the word.
branches.cn: 果实线：圆果是这个词的中心。

branches.en: THE TREE LINE: the bearer shares the name of what it bears.
branches.cn: 果树线：结出果实的树共享果实的名字。

branches.en: THE EYE LINE: the pupil was once an apple, so a loved one sits at the centre of sight.
branches.cn: 眼睛线：瞳孔曾被称作苹果，于是所爱的人坐在视线中心。

branches.en: THE THROAT LINE: the lump is imagined as the fruit that stuck.
branches.cn: 喉部线：喉结被想象成卡住的那枚果子。

branches.en: THE CITY LINE: jazz gave New York a fruit nickname.
branches.cn: 城市线：爵士乐给了纽约一个水果绰号。

intro.en: Apple is a native Germanic word, so its own structure is simple; the compounds below show how it joins other words.
intro.cn: apple 是本土的日耳曼词，自身结构简单；下面的复合词展示它如何与其他词结合。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin layer in apple: the word is Germanic, and the Latin fruit words are unrelated.
latinIntro.cn: apple 没有拉丁层：这个词属于日耳曼语，拉丁语的水果词与它并无亲缘关系。

definition_zh: 申请；申请书；应用；运用；应用程序；涂抹；敷用；勤奋；专心
definition_en: a formal request, the act of putting something to use, a computer program, or the act of spreading something on a surface
core_image: 一张写满理由的表格被递到窗口，随后又被拿去用起来
scene: 招聘窗口前，年轻人把一叠材料塞进信封。She sent her application to the university before the deadline.
sceneCN: 这里 application 是「申请；申请书」（第 1 个义项：向机构提出的正式请求）；句意为「她在截止日期前把申请寄给了大学」。画面里有招聘窗口、信封与一叠材料。

pos.zh: 名词：申请；申请书；应用；运用；应用程序；涂抹；勤奋

derivatives.zh: 由 apply 加 -ant 构成，义为「申请人」
由 apply 加 -able 构成，义为「适用的；相关的」
由 apply 加 -ator 构成，义为「涂抹器；敷料器」
由 applicable 加 -ity 构成，义为「适用性」

senses.title: A formal request
senses.definition: a formal written or spoken request, especially for a job, a place, or permission
senses.definitionCN: 为职位、名额或许可提出的正式书面或口头请求
senses.example: Her application for the scholarship arrived on time.
senses.exampleCN: 她的奖学金申请按时寄到了。
senses.why: Latin applicare meant to attach one thing to another; a request attaches a person to a post or a place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 applicare 意为把一物贴附到另一物上；一份申请就是把一个人附到一个职位或一个地方上。

senses.title: Putting something to use
senses.definition: the act of putting a rule, method, or idea to practical use
senses.definitionCN: 把规则、方法或想法投入实际使用的行为
senses.example: The application of this rule to real cases is not always simple.
senses.exampleCN: 把这条规则应用到真实案例上并不总是简单。
senses.why: The same image of attaching remains: an idea is fastened onto a real situation and made to work there.
senses.whyCN: 「贴附」的意象仍在：一种想法被固定到真实处境上，并在那里起作用。

senses.title: A computer program
senses.definition: a computer program designed for a particular task, especially on a phone or tablet
senses.definitionCN: 为特定任务设计的计算机程序，尤指手机或平板上的程序
senses.example: She installed a language application on her phone.
senses.exampleCN: 她在手机上装了一个语言学习程序。
senses.why: The program is attached to a task the way a tool is applied to work.
senses.whyCN: 程序被贴附到一项任务上，正如工具被用于工作。

senses.title: Spreading a substance
senses.definition: the act of spreading a substance such as cream or paint onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把药膏、涂料一类物质铺到表面上的动作
senses.example: The application of the ointment should be repeated twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药膏应每天涂抹两次。
senses.why: Here applicare is literal: the substance is laid directly onto the skin.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 applicare 是字面义：物质被直接敷到皮肤上。

senses.title: Close attention to work
senses.definition: the quality of working hard and giving close attention to a task
senses.definitionCN: 努力工作并对任务保持专注的品质
senses.example: Success in the course depends on steady application.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课能否学好，取决于能否持续用功。
senses.why: To apply oneself is to attach the whole mind to the work, and the noun keeps that image of close attachment.
senses.whyCN: 投入自己就是把整个心思贴附到工作上，这个名词保留的正是那种紧密贴附的意象。

intro.en: Application is built on the Latin verb applicare, and its whole history is the history of attaching one thing to another.
intro.cn: application 建立在拉丁语动词 applicare 之上，它的整段历史就是「把一物贴到另一物」的历史。

items.en: 「*plek-」 is reconstructed with the sense 'to weave, plait, fold'. The deeper origin of this root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 原始印欧语「*plek-」被重构为「编织、折叠」的意思；这个更早的来源存疑。

items.en: Plicare meant 'to fold', and its compounds carry the idea of laying one thing onto another.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」，它的复合词带有把一物铺到另一物上的意思。

items.en: Ad- plus plicare gave applicare, 'to attach, put to, apply'; the noun applicatio follows the same pattern.
items.cn: ad- 与 plicare 构成 applicare，意为「贴附、施加、应用」；名词 applicatio 沿同一路径而来。

items.en: Old French aplier and its derived noun enter English usage after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 aplier 及其派生名词在诺曼时期之后进入英语用法。

items.en: The word splits into a request, a use, a coating, a program and a habit of diligence.
items.cn: 这个词分成申请、运用、涂抹、程序与勤奋几种用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the family built on apply; the near-meaning group gathers words for requests, use and diligence.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 apply 之上的一族词；近义组收表示请求、使用与勤奋的词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, meaning to request, use, or spread.
entries.definitionCN: 本词由它加后缀构成，义为「申请、使用、涂抹」的动词。

entries.definition: A person who makes a formal request.
entries.definitionCN: 提出正式申请的人，即「申请人」。

entries.definition: Able to be applied or relevant to a particular case.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「适用的、相关的」。

entries.definition: A device for spreading a substance on a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「涂抹器、敷料器」。

entries.definition: An act of asking for something in a polite or formal way.
entries.definitionCN: 以礼貌或正式方式提出请求的行为，对应 application 的申请义。

entries.definition: A formal written appeal, often signed by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 常由多人签名的正式书面请愿，与申请书相近。

entries.definition: The way in which something is used, or the amount of use.
entries.definitionCN: 某物被使用的方式或使用量，对应 application 的应用义。

entries.definition: Careful and persistent effort in work.
entries.definitionCN: 工作中细心而持续的努力，对应 application 的勤奋义。

normalIntro.en: The hooks follow the Latin image of attaching one thing to another.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子沿着拉丁语「把一物贴到另一物」的意象展开。

normal.en: Apply plus -ation: the noun of putting something to work.
normal.cn: apply 加 -ation：把某物拿去用的名词。

normal.en: A request attaches you to a post: a job application.
normal.cn: 申请把你附到一个职位上：求职申请。

normal.en: An idea attached to reality is its application.
normal.cn: 想法贴到现实上，就是它的应用。

normal.en: A program is a tool attached to a task.
normal.cn: 程序是被贴到任务上的工具。

normal.en: Applying yourself means attaching the whole mind.
normal.cn: 投入自己就是把整个心思贴上去。

abstract.en: One verb of attaching yields a form, a use, a program and a virtue.
abstract.cn: 一个表示贴附的动词，生出表格、用途、程序与美德。

abstract.en: The word always joins two things: person and post, rule and case.
abstract.cn: 这个词总在连接两样东西：人与职位、规则与案例。

abstract.en: Its range shows how paperwork and technology share one image.
abstract.cn: 它的范围显示文书与技术共享同一个意象。

examples.en: She sent her application to the university before the deadline.
examples.cn: 她在截止日期前把申请寄给了大学。

examples.en: The application of this rule to real cases is not always simple.
examples.cn: 把这条规则应用到真实案例上并不总是简单。

examples.en: He praised her steady application to the research.
examples.cn: 他称赞她对研究持续用功。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普里凯申」——把一张申请表贴在职位门口：申请；应用

root: application 来自拉丁语 applicare「贴附、施加」，该动词由 ad-「向」与 plicare「折叠」构成，更早的印欧词根形式存疑。经古法语进入英语后，这个词一方面指把请求递交上去的申请与申请书，另一方面指把规则、想法、药膏贴到对象上的应用与涂抹；现代又添了计算机应用程序与勤奋、专心两层用法。

sensesIntro.en: Five uses all keep the Latin image of attaching: a request, a rule put to work, a program, a cream spread on skin, and a mind fixed on study.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个用法都保留拉丁语「贴附」的意象：一份请求、一条被拿去用的规则、一个程序、一层涂在皮肤上的药膏，以及一颗钉在学业上的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a filled form pressed onto a desk, then a tool pressed onto a task.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张填好的表格被按到桌上，随后工具被按到任务上。

branches.en: THE REQUEST LINE: a person is attached to a post or a place.
branches.cn: 申请线：一个人被附到一个职位或一个地方上。

branches.en: THE USE LINE: an idea is attached to a real situation.
branches.cn: 运用线：一种想法被贴附到真实处境上。

branches.en: THE PROGRAM LINE: a tool is attached to a task.
branches.cn: 程序线：工具被贴附到一项任务上。

branches.en: THE COATING LINE: a substance is laid onto a surface.
branches.cn: 涂抹线：物质被铺到表面上。

branches.en: THE DILIGENCE LINE: the whole mind is attached to the work.
branches.cn: 勤奋线：整个心思被贴附到工作上。

intro.en: Application is a transparent derivative of apply: the verb plus the noun suffix -ation.
intro.cn: application 是 apply 的透明派生词：动词加名词后缀 -ation。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is real: applicare 'attach' and plicare 'fold' are the ancestors of the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是真实的：applicare「贴附」与 plicare「折叠」是这个词的祖先。

items.meaning: a request or the act of applying
items.example: The application was approved within a week.

senses.title: To make a formal request
senses.definition: to make a formal request for a job, a place, a grant, or permission
senses.definitionCN: 为职位、名额、补助或许可提出正式请求
senses.example: She applied for a place in the design programme.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了设计专业的一个名额。
senses.why: Latin applicare first meant to attach oneself to something, and a request is the act of attaching yourself to a post.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 applicare 最初意为把自己贴附到某物上，而申请就是把自己附到一个职位上的动作。

senses.title: To put something to use
senses.definition: to use a rule, method, skill, or idea in a particular situation
senses.definitionCN: 在特定情境中使用规则、方法、技能或想法
senses.example: Try to apply the same method to the next problem.
senses.exampleCN: 试着把同样的方法用到下一道题上。
senses.why: A method is folded onto a case, the way one layer is laid over another surface.
senses.whyCN: 方法被折叠到案例上，就像一层东西铺在另一层表面上。

senses.title: To spread on a surface
senses.definition: to spread or rub a substance such as cream, paint, or medicine onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把药膏、涂料或药物铺开、擦到某个表面上
senses.example: Apply the cream thinly twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 每天薄薄地涂两次药膏。
senses.why: This is applicare at its most physical: the substance is laid directly onto the skin.
senses.whyCN: 这是 applicare 最物理的用法：物质被直接铺到皮肤上。

senses.title: To be relevant
senses.definition: to be relevant to or valid for a person, case, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某案例或某情境相关并有效
senses.example: The rule applies to every member of the team.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规则适用于队里的每一个人。
senses.why: Where a rule can be attached, it holds; being applicable is being able to be laid on the case.
senses.whyCN: 规则能被贴附到哪儿，就在哪儿生效；所谓适用，就是能被铺到那个案例上。

senses.title: To devote oneself
senses.definition: to work hard and give close attention to a task
senses.definitionCN: 努力工作并对一项任务保持专注
senses.example: If you apply yourself, the exam should go well.
senses.exampleCN: 如果你肯用功，这次考试应该会顺利。
senses.why: To apply oneself is to attach the whole mind to the task, leaving nothing loose.
senses.whyCN: 投入自己就是把整个心思贴到任务上，不留一点松散。

intro.en: Apply comes from the Latin verb of attaching, and every sense still carries that gesture.
intro.cn: apply 来自那个表示贴附的拉丁语动词，每个义项都还带着这个动作。

items.en: 「*plek-」 'to weave, fold' is the reconstructed root; its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 原始印欧语「*plek-」意为「编织、折叠」，是重构的词根；更早的来源存疑。

items.en: Plicare 'to fold' supplies the physical image of one layer laid over another.
items.cn: plicare「折叠」提供了一层铺到另一层上的物理意象。

items.en: Ad- plus plicare formed applicare, 'to attach, put to, apply'.
items.cn: ad- 与 plicare 构成 applicare，意为「贴附、施加、应用」。

items.en: French aplier carries the verb into English, where it loses the final Latin ending.
items.cn: 法语 aplier 把这个动词带进英语，拉丁词尾在这里脱落。

items.en: The single verb spreads into requests, uses, coatings, relevance and hard study.
items.cn: 这一个动词铺开成申请、使用、涂抹、适用与用功。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun family built on apply; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of using, asking and spreading.
note.cn: 形近组收由 apply 构成的名词族；近义组收表示使用、请求与涂抹的动词。

scene: 董事会散会后，主席在走廊上停下脚步宣布人选。The board appointed her as the new director of research.
sceneCN: 这里 appoint 是「任命；委派」（第 1 个义项：把某人指定到某个职位上）；句意为「董事会任命她为新的研究主管」。画面里有散会的成员、长长的走廊与主席手中的名册。

senses.title: To name someone for a post
senses.definition: to officially choose someone for a job, office, or duty
senses.definitionCN: 正式选定某人担任某项工作、职务或职责
senses.example: The board appointed her as the new director of research.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会任命她为新的研究主管。
senses.why: Old French apointer put a person at a point, and a post is exactly such a point in an organization.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 apointer 把人放到某个点上，而职位正是组织里的这样一个点。

senses.title: To fix a time or place
senses.definition: to arrange or fix a time and place for something by agreement
senses.definitionCN: 经双方同意安排或确定某事的时间与地点
senses.example: They appointed a day for the next meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他们约定了下次会议的日期。
senses.why: A time is also a point on the calendar; to appoint it is to fix it by agreement.
senses.whyCN: 时间也是日历上的一个点；约定时间就是经双方同意把它固定下来。

senses.title: Something settled in advance
senses.definition: in phrases such as the appointed hour, a time or place already fixed
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the appointed hour 一类说法，指已经确定的时间或地点
senses.example: The appointed hour came and no one arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 约定的时间到了，却没有人来。
senses.why: Once a point is fixed, whatever is to happen at it has been decided in advance.
senses.whyCN: 一个点一旦被固定，在这个点上要发生什么就被预先决定了。

senses.title: To furnish and equip
senses.definition: to supply a room or building with furniture and equipment, an older use of the word
senses.definitionCN: 为房间或建筑配置家具与设备，属于较古的用法
senses.example: The hall was appointed with heavy oak tables.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅里配置了厚重的橡木桌。
senses.why: The older sense furnished a place by placing each item at its proper point.
senses.whyCN: 较古的义项是把每件东西放到它应在的位置上，从而布置好一个地方。

intro.en: Appoint comes from the French phrase for putting something at a point, and the point is still visible in its senses.
intro.cn: appoint 来自法语中「把某物放到一个点上」的说法，那个点至今仍留在它的各个义项里。

items.en: 「*peuǵ-」 'to prick, point' is the reconstructed root behind the point words; its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 原始印欧语「*peuǵ-」意为「刺、点」，是这一族「点」类词的根源；更早的来源存疑。

items.en: Punctum means 'a point, a prick', from the verb pungere 'to prick'.
items.cn: punctum 意为「点、刺痕」，来自动词 pungere「刺」。

items.en: French point means both a point and a fixed spot or moment.
items.cn: 法语 point 既指一个点，也指固定的地点或时刻。

items.en: Apointer, 'to put at a point, to arrange', gives English appoint in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: apointer 意为「放到一个点上、安排」，十四世纪时进入英语成为 appoint。

items.en: The sense of naming someone to a post dominates; the older sense of furnishing survives only in old texts.
items.cn: 任命某人担任职位的义项占了主导；较古的布置义只留在旧文献里。

note.cn: 形近组收 appoint 的派生词族；近义组收表示挑选与确定的动词。

normalIntro.en: The hooks all return to the picture of a point on a page or a calendar.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子都回到纸面或日历上的一个点。

normal.en: A point is the heart of the word: appoint means put at a point.
normal.cn: 点是这个词的核心：appoint 就是把某物放到一个点上。

normal.en: Put a name at the point of a post, and you have appointed someone.
normal.cn: 把名字放到职位这个点上，你就任命了某人。

normal.en: Put a meeting at a point on the calendar, and you have appointed a day.

abstract.cn: 一个点可以放名字、放时刻，也可以放一件家具。

abstract.en: Appointing is always an act of fixing: who, when, where.
abstract.cn: 任命与约定都是一种固定：定人、定时、定地。

abstract.en: The word turns empty space into an order.
abstract.cn: 这个词把空处变成一个秩序。

root: appoint 来自古法语 apointer「放到一个点上、安排」，其源头是拉丁语 punctum「点」，再往上可追到表示「刺、点」的印欧词根，确切形式存疑。十四世纪进入英语后，这个词始终围绕「把一个点固定下来」：把名字放到职位这个点上就是任命，把会议放到日历这个点上就是约定，把时间地点提前钉死就是指定的，而较古的用法是把家具各放到应在的点位上，也就是布置。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses all fix something at a point: a person to a post, a meeting to a day, an hour already settled, and furniture placed in a room.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法都把某物固定在一个点上：把人定到职位，把会议定到某日，把时间提前钉死，以及把家具摆进房间。

branches.en: THE POST LINE: a name is fixed to a position.

branches.en: THE ORDER LINE: people and times are arranged into a plan.
branches.cn: 秩序线：人与时间被编排进一个计划。

core_image: 日历上圈出的一个时刻，有人在那个点上等你
scene: 诊所前台，护士翻开登记本，在某一页写下一行。She had an appointment with the dentist at four o'clock.
sceneCN: 这里 appointment 是「约会；预约」（第 1 个义项：约定在固定时间见面的安排）；句意为「她四点与牙医有预约」。画面里有诊所前台、登记本与候诊椅。

pos.zh: 名词：约会；预约；任命；委任；职位；职务

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -ment 得到的动词，义为「任命；约定」
由 appoint 加 -ee 构成，义为「被任命者」

由 dis- 加 appoint 再加 -ment 构成，义为「失望」

senses.title: An arranged meeting
senses.definition: an arrangement to meet someone or be at a place at a fixed time
senses.definitionCN: 约定在固定时间与某人见面或到某地的安排
senses.example: She had an appointment with the dentist at four o'clock.
senses.exampleCN: 她四点与牙医有预约。
senses.why: The word carries the French point: a fixed point of time at which two people are to meet.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着法语那个「点」：两个人要在某个固定的时间点上见面。

senses.title: The act of naming to a post
senses.definition: the act of officially choosing someone for a job or office
senses.definitionCN: 正式选定某人担任某项工作或职务的行为
senses.example: His appointment as chief engineer surprised the staff.
senses.exampleCN: 他被任命为总工程师，让员工们吃了一惊。
senses.why: The same noun names the act of putting a name at the point of a post.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也命名把名字放到职位这个点上的动作。

senses.title: The post itself
senses.definition: the job or office to which someone has been appointed
senses.definitionCN: 某人被任命担任的工作或职务本身
senses.example: She took up her appointment in the autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 她在秋天就任了这个职位。
senses.why: The point at which the person was placed becomes the place itself.
senses.whyCN: 人被放到的那个点，随后就成了那个位置本身。

senses.title: Furnishings, in the plural
senses.definition: in the plural and in older usage, the furniture and equipment of a room or building
senses.definitionCN: 用于复数且属较古用法，指房间或建筑内的家具与设备
senses.example: The appointments of the old library were sold at auction.
senses.exampleCN: 旧图书馆的家具设备被拍卖掉了。
senses.why: The old sense of furnishing a place survives in the plural, where each object sits at its appointed spot.
senses.whyCN: 布置一个地方的古老义项留在复数里，每件东西都坐在为它指定的点位上。

intro.en: Appointment is appoint plus the noun suffix -ment, and it inherits the French idea of a fixed point.
intro.cn: appointment 是 appoint 加名词后缀 -ment，继承了法语中「固定的一点」的观念。

items.en: Punctum 'a point' comes from pungere 'to prick', and it gives French its word for a point.
items.cn: punctum「点」来自 pungere「刺」，它给法语提供了表示「点」的词。

items.en: Apointer 'to put at a point, arrange' is the verb behind the whole English family.
items.cn: apointer「放到一个点上、安排」是整族英语词背后的动词。

items.en: English appointen appears in the fourteenth century with the sense of arranging or naming.
items.cn: 英语 appointen 在十四世纪出现，带有安排或指定的意思。

items.en: The noun suffix -ment turns the verb into either the act or the thing arranged.
items.cn: 名词后缀 -ment 把动词转成动作本身，或转成被安排好的事物。

items.en: The noun covers a diary entry, a named post and, in the plural, the furniture of a room.
items.cn: 这个名词覆盖日历上的一条约会、一个被任命的职位，以及复数形式下的一屋子家具。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on appoint; the near-meaning group gathers words for meetings and posts.
note.cn: 形近组收由 appoint 构成的词；近义组收表示会面与职位的词。

entries.definitionCN: 本词由它加 -ment 构成，义为「任命、约定」的动词。

entries.definition: A person who has been given a post.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「被任命者」。

entries.definition: To fail to meet a hope or expectation.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使失望」，与 appoint 形近而义远。

entries.definition: Fixed or chosen in advance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「约定的、被任命的」。

entries.definition: An occasion when people come together.
entries.definitionCN: 人们聚在一起的场合，比 appointment 更不强调事先约定。

entries.definition: A formal arrangement to be somewhere at a time.
entries.definitionCN: 在某个时间到某个地方的正式安排，与 appointment 最近。

entries.definition: A period of time set aside for a particular activity.
entries.definitionCN: 为某项活动留出的一段时间，如诊疗或授课。

entries.definition: A job to which someone is sent, especially abroad.
entries.definitionCN: 被派去担任的职位，尤指驻外职位，对应 appointment 的职位义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a circled point in a diary.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子始终围绕日历上被圈出的那个点。

normal.en: Appoint plus -ment: the thing fixed at a point.
normal.cn: appoint 加 -ment：被固定在某个点上的那件事。

normal.en: A meeting fixed at a point is an appointment.
normal.cn: 固定在某个点上的会面，就是预约。

normal.en: A name fixed at a post is also an appointment.
normal.cn: 固定在职位上的名字，也是任命。

normal.en: The post is the point where the name was placed.

normal.en: Old furnishings each had their appointed spot.
normal.cn: 旧时的家具各有自己被指定的位置。

abstract.en: One noun holds a time, a job and a room full of furniture.
abstract.cn: 一个名词装着一段时间、一份工作与一屋子家具。

abstract.en: All three are points where something has been fixed.
abstract.cn: 这三者都是某物被固定下来的点。

abstract.en: The word makes arrangement visible as a mark on a page.
abstract.cn: 这个词让「安排」变成纸面上的一个记号。

examples.en: She had an appointment with the dentist at four o'clock.
examples.cn: 她四点与牙医有预约。

examples.en: His appointment as chief engineer surprised the staff.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿波因特门特」——日历上点一个点，写上时间与人名：预约；任命

root: appointment 由 appoint 加名词后缀 -ment 构成。appoint 来自古法语 apointer「放到一个点上、安排」，源头是拉丁语 punctum「点」。因此这个名词的三层主要意思都围绕同一个点：把会面放到时间这个点上，就是预约；把名字放到职位这个点上，就是任命；被放到的那个点本身，就是职位。复数形式还保留了较古的布置义，指一屋子里各就其位的家具设备。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses all fix something at a point: a meeting in a diary, a person named to a post, the post itself, and furniture placed in a room.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法都把某物固定在一个点上：日历里的会面、被任命到职位的人、职位本身，以及摆进房间的家具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a time circled in a diary, with a name written inside the circle.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历上被圈出的一个时刻，圈里写着一个名字。

branches.en: THE DIARY LINE: two people are fixed to one hour.
branches.cn: 日历线：两个人被固定到同一个小时上。

branches.en: THE NAMING LINE: a person is fixed to a post.
branches.cn: 任命线：一个人被固定到一个职位上。

branches.en: THE POST LINE: the fixed point becomes a place to work.
branches.cn: 职位线：被固定的那个点变成工作的位置。

branches.en: THE ROOM LINE: objects each sit at their appointed spot.
branches.cn: 房间线：每件东西都坐在为它指定的位置上。

branches.en: THE ORDER LINE: times and people are arranged into a plan.
branches.cn: 秩序线：时间与人被编排进一个计划。

intro.en: Appointment is a transparent suffix noun, and its stems are all visible inside it.
intro.cn: appointment 是透明的后缀名词，它的各个词干都还能在词里看见。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is punctum 'point', which sits behind the French verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 punctum「点」，它位于法语动词背后。

items.meaning: a fixed meeting or a named post
items.example: The appointment was moved to Monday.
items.exampleCN: 预约被改到了周一。

items.example: They appoint a new coach every year.

items.meaning: forming nouns of act or result
items.meaningCN: 构成表示行为或结果的名词后缀
items.example: It turns the verb into a settled thing.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词转成一件已成定局的事。

items.example: Please make an appointment before you visit.
items.exampleCN: 来访前请先预约。

items.example: The gallery is open by appointment.

items.example: The receptionist opened the appointment book.
items.exampleCN: 前台翻开了预约登记本。

definition_zh: 感激；感谢；欣赏；赏识；理解；意识到；增值；涨价
definition_en: to be grateful for something, to recognize the value or quality of something, to understand fully, or to rise in value
core_image: 把一件东西放上天平，认真称出它值多少
scene: 画展里，观众在一幅旧画前站了很久。She stood before the painting and began to appreciate its quiet colours.
sceneCN: 这里 appreciate 是「欣赏；赏识」（第 2 个义项：认识到某物的价值与好处）；句意为「她站在画前，开始欣赏它沉静的色彩」。画面里有一幅旧画、驻足观看的观众与展厅的灯光。

pos.zh: 动词：感激；欣赏；理解；增值

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ation 构成，义为「感激；欣赏；理解；增值」
由本词加 -ative 构成，义为「感激的；有欣赏力的」
由本词加 -able 构成，义为「可观的；明显的」
由 de- 加同一词根构成，义为「贬值；贬低」

senses.title: To be grateful for something
senses.definition: to feel thankful for something someone has done
senses.definitionCN: 对别人所做之事心怀感谢
senses.example: I really appreciate your help with the move.
senses.exampleCN: 我非常感谢你帮我搬家。
senses.why: Latin appretiare meant to set a price on something; gratitude is a way of setting a high value on what was given.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 appretiare 意为给某物定价；感激就是给所受的给予估一个很高的价值。

senses.title: To recognize the worth of something
senses.definition: to recognize and enjoy the value or quality of something
senses.definitionCN: 认识到并享受某物的价值或品质
senses.example: She stood before the painting and began to appreciate its quiet colours.
senses.exampleCN: 她站在画前，开始欣赏它沉静的色彩。
senses.why: To appreciate art is to weigh its worth and find it great.
senses.whyCN: 欣赏艺术就是称量它的价值，并发现它很重。

senses.title: To understand fully
senses.definition: to understand fully how serious, important, or difficult something is
senses.definitionCN: 充分理解某事有多严重、重要或困难
senses.example: Few drivers appreciate how dangerous ice can be.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有司机真正意识到冰面有多危险。
senses.why: Full understanding is a correct valuation: seeing a thing at its true weight.
senses.whyCN: 充分理解是一种正确的估价：按它真正的分量来看待一件事。

senses.title: To rise in value
senses.definition: to increase in value or price over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间推移价值或价格上升
senses.example: The old house has appreciated sharply in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋老房子在十年间大幅增值。
senses.why: Here the price is literal and it rises; the word returns to its money root.
senses.whyCN: 这里的价格是字面的，而且往上涨；这个词回到了它关于钱的词根。

intro.en: Appreciate is built on the Latin word for price, and every sense is some kind of weighing.
intro.cn: appreciate 建立在拉丁语的「价格」一词上，每个义项都是某种称量。

items.en: Pretium means 'price, value', and its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: pretium 意为「价格、价值」，它更早的来源存疑。

items.en: Ad- plus pretiare 'to price' produced appretiare, 'to set a value on'.
items.cn: ad- 与 pretiare「定价」构成 appretiare，意为「给……估价」。

items.en: French apprécier carries both 'to value' and 'to be grateful for'.
items.cn: 法语 apprécier 同时带有「估价」与「感激」两层意思。

items.en: English appreciate arrives in the sixteenth century with the sense of valuing or estimating.
items.cn: 英语 appreciate 在十六世纪进入英语，带有估价、判断价值的意思。

items.en: The money sense 'rise in value' develops later and runs beside the moral senses.
items.cn: 「增值」这条关于钱的义项较晚出现，与那些关于品行的义项并行。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the price root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of valuing and understanding.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在「价格」词根上的词；近义组收表示估价与理解的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for gratitude, enjoyment, or a rise in value.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词派生的名词，义为「感激、欣赏、增值」。

entries.definition: Showing gratitude or enjoying quality.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「感激的；有欣赏力的」。

entries.definition: Large enough to be noticed or measured.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可观的、明显的」，仍带「可估量」的原意。

entries.definition: To fall in value or to speak of something as worthless.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「贬值；贬低」，与 appreciate 反向。

entries.definition: To regard something as important or worthwhile.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「重视、珍视」，对应 appreciate 的赏识义。

entries.definition: To regard someone or something with respect and pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 带着敬意与愉悦看待某人某物，比 appreciate 更偏情感。

entries.definition: To grasp the meaning or seriousness of something.
entries.definitionCN: 理解某事的含义或严重性，对应 appreciate 的理解义。

entries.definition: To keep and value something highly.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物珍藏并高度看重，情感比 appreciate 更浓。

normalIntro.en: These hooks all use the price root preci and the image of weighing worth.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子都用「价格」词根 preci 与称量价值的意象。

normal.en: Preci means price: appreciate is to put a price on worth.
normal.cn: preci 意为价格：appreciate 就是给价值定个价。

normal.en: Thanking someone is pricing their kindness high.
normal.cn: 感谢别人，就是把他的好意估得很高。

normal.en: Enjoying a painting is weighing its quality.
normal.cn: 欣赏一幅画，就是称量它的品质。

normal.en: Understanding a danger is seeing its true weight.
normal.cn: 理解一种危险，就是看见它真实的分量。

normal.en: A house that appreciates literally gains price.
normal.cn: 增值的房子就是字面上涨了价。

abstract.en: The same scale measures kindness, beauty, danger and money.
abstract.cn: 同一架天平称量善意、美、危险与金钱。

abstract.en: Appreciation is always an act of seeing worth.
abstract.cn: 欣赏与感激，归根到底都是看见价值。

abstract.en: The word teaches that valuing is a kind of knowledge.
abstract.cn: 这个词告诉我们：懂得看重，本身也是一种认识。

examples.en: I really appreciate your help with the move.
examples.cn: 我非常感谢你帮我搬家。

examples.en: She stood before the painting and began to appreciate its quiet colours.
examples.cn: 她站在画前，开始欣赏它沉静的色彩。

examples.en: Few drivers appreciate how dangerous ice can be.
examples.cn: 很少有司机真正意识到冰面有多危险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普瑞希埃特」——把东西放上天平，称出它值多少：感激；欣赏

root: appreciate 来自拉丁语 appretiare「给……估价」，该动词由 ad- 与 pretium「价格、价值」构成，pretium 更早的来源存疑。经法语 apprécier 进入英语后，这个词始终在做同一件事：称量价值。给别人的帮助称出很高的价值，就是感激；给一件作品称出很高的价值，就是欣赏；把危险按真实分量称出来，就是理解；而价格本身往上走，就是增值。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses all weigh worth: gratitude prices kindness high, appreciation prices beauty high, understanding sees true weight, and rising value is literal price.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法都在称量价值：感激把善意估高，欣赏把美估高，理解看见真实分量，而增值则是字面上的价格上升。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of scales with a thing on one side and its worth on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平，一边放东西，另一边放它的价值。

branches.en: THE GRATITUDE LINE: kindness is priced high.
branches.cn: 感激线：别人的善意被估得很高。

branches.en: THE BEAUTY LINE: quality is weighed and enjoyed.
branches.cn: 美感线：品质被称量并被享受。

branches.en: THE KNOWLEDGE LINE: a danger is seen at its true weight.
branches.cn: 认识线：危险被按真实分量看见。

branches.en: THE MARKET LINE: the price itself goes up.
branches.cn: 市场线：价格本身往上走。

branches.en: THE MORAL LINE: both gratitude and taste are forms of valuing.
branches.cn: 品行线：感激与品味都是看重价值的方式。

intro.en: Appreciate is a Latin word for pricing, and its family keeps the root preci visible.
intro.cn: appreciate 是一个表示定价的拉丁词，词族里仍能看见词根 preci。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is real: pretium 'price' lies inside appretiare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是真实的：pretium「价格」就在 appretiare 里面。

items.meaning: to value, be grateful, or rise
items.example: We appreciate your patience.
items.exampleCN: 我们感谢你的耐心。

items.example: Her appreciation of the gift was genuine.
items.exampleCN: 她对这份礼物的感激是真诚的。

items.example: The audience was warmly appreciative.
items.exampleCN: 观众热情地表示欣赏。

items.example: There was an appreciable drop in noise.
items.exampleCN: 噪音有明显的下降。

items.example: The room grew appreciably cooler.
items.exampleCN: 房间明显变凉了。

items.example: Cars depreciate quickly.
items.exampleCN: 汽车贬值很快。

items.example: The price rose again this spring.
items.exampleCN: 价格今年春天又涨了。

items.example: Water is precious in the desert.
items.exampleCN: 在沙漠里，水很珍贵。

definition_zh: 接近；靠近；临近；方法；途径；处理；对付；通路；入口
definition_en: to come near a place, person, or time; a way of dealing with something; or the path that leads to a place
core_image: 脚步一步步靠近一扇门，手里还带着一套办法
scene: 山路上，两个人迎着晨雾向村子走去。As they approached the village, the church bell began to ring.
sceneCN: 这里 approach 是「接近；靠近」（第 1 个义项：在空间上向某处移动、靠近）；句意为「他们走近村子时，教堂的钟开始响」。画面里有蜿蜒的山路、晨雾与远处的村庄。

pos.zh: 动词：接近；靠近；临近；处理；对付
名词：方法；途径；通路；入口

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -able 构成，义为「平易近人的；可接近的」
由 un- 加 approachable 构成，义为「难以接近的；冷淡的」
由 approachable 加 -ity 构成，义为「可接近性；亲切」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「即将到来的」

senses.title: To move nearer
senses.definition: to move nearer to a place, person, or object
senses.definitionCN: 在空间上向某地、某人或某物移动得更近
senses.example: As they approached the village, the church bell began to ring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们走近村子时，教堂的钟开始响。
senses.why: Late Latin appropiare joined ad- 'to' with prope 'near'; the verb is simply the act of getting nearer.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 appropiare 把 ad-「向」与 prope「近」连起来；这个动词就是变得更近的动作。

senses.title: A way of dealing with something
senses.definition: a way of dealing with a problem or of doing a task
senses.definitionCN: 处理问题或完成任务的某种方式
senses.example: The teacher tried a different approach to reading.
senses.exampleCN: 老师尝试了一种不同的阅读教学法。
senses.why: A path that leads to a place becomes a path that leads to a solution.
senses.whyCN: 通向一个地点的路径，变成了通向一个解法的路径。

senses.title: To begin dealing with
senses.definition: to begin to deal with a problem, task, or person in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式开始处理问题、任务或某人
senses.example: We need to approach the question from the data.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要从数据出发来处理这个问题。
senses.why: Coming near a problem is the first step of handling it.
senses.whyCN: 靠近一个问题，就是处理它的第一步。

senses.title: To come close in time
senses.definition: to come close in time, as a season, event, or deadline
senses.definitionCN: 在时间上临近，如季节、事件或截止日期
senses.example: As winter approaches, the nights grow longer.
senses.exampleCN: 随着冬天临近，夜变得更长。
senses.why: The space word is applied to the calendar: a season also draws near.
senses.whyCN: 空间词被用到日历上：一个季节也会逐渐靠近。

senses.title: The road that leads in
senses.definition: the road, path, or way by which one reaches a place
senses.definitionCN: 抵达某处所经的道路、路径或通道
senses.example: The approach to the castle was steep and narrow.
senses.exampleCN: 通往城堡的路又陡又窄。
senses.why: The noun keeps the physical path that the verb travels along.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留的正是动词所走的那条实体路径。

intro.en: Approach comes from the Latin words for 'near', and it moves easily from space to time to method.
intro.cn: approach 来自拉丁语中表示「近」的词，并从空间自然滑向时间与方法。

items.en: Prope means 'near', and it supplies the whole family with its idea of closeness.
items.cn: prope 意为「近」，它为整族词提供了「接近」的观念。

items.en: Ad- plus prope formed appropiare, 'to come near to'.
items.cn: ad- 与 prope 构成 appropiare，意为「靠近」。

items.en: French aprochier carries the verb into English with the same physical sense.
items.cn: 法语 aprochier 把这个动词带进英语，仍保留同样的空间义。

items.en: English approchen appears in the fourteenth century; the noun follows soon after.
items.cn: 英语 approchen 在十四世纪出现，名词紧随其后。

items.en: The word extends from walking nearer to the method one takes toward a problem.
items.cn: 这个词从走近某处扩展到面对问题时采取的方法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the approach family and a near-spelling trap; the near-meaning group gathers words for method and access.
note.cn: 形近组收 approach 的词族与一个拼写陷阱；近义组收表示方法与通道的词。

entries.definition: Easy to meet and talk to.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「平易近人的」，由本词加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: Hard to meet or too distant in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以接近的、冷淡的」。

entries.definition: To express blame or disappointment to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「责备、指责」，与 approach 形近而义远。

entries.definition: A planned way of doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 做事的计划性方式，对应 approach 的方法义。

entries.definition: A manner of doing something or a route.
entries.definitionCN: 做事的方式或路线，一词兼有方法与通路两义。

entries.definition: At a short distance in space or time.
entries.definitionCN: 空间或时间上距离很短，对应 approach 的接近义。

entries.definition: The means or right of reaching a place.
entries.definitionCN: 抵达某处的手段或权利，对应 approach 的通路义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the feet moving nearer, then turn the road into a method.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子先跟着脚步靠近，再把那条路变成方法。

normal.en: Approach begins with feet: to come nearer.
normal.cn: approach 从脚开始：走近。

normal.en: The road you take in is also an approach.
normal.cn: 你走进去的那条路，也叫 approach。

normal.en: The way you take toward a problem is your approach.
normal.cn: 你走向问题的方式，就是你的方法。

normal.en: A season can approach without any feet.
normal.cn: 季节可以在没有脚步的情况下临近。

normal.en: Approachable people are easy to come near.
normal.cn: 平易近人的人，很容易靠近。

abstract.en: Nearness becomes both a road and a method.
abstract.cn: 「近」既变成一条路，也变成一种方法。

abstract.en: The word shows that handling a problem starts with coming close to it.
abstract.cn: 这个词显示，处理问题的第一步是靠近它。

abstract.en: Space, time and thought share one verb.
abstract.cn: 空间、时间与思路共用一个动词。

examples.en: As they approached the village, the church bell began to ring.
examples.cn: 他们走近村子时，教堂的钟开始响。

examples.en: The teacher tried a different approach to reading.
examples.cn: 老师尝试了一种不同的阅读教学法。

examples.en: The approach to the castle was steep and narrow.
examples.cn: 通往城堡的路又陡又窄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普罗奇」——脚步一步一步靠近那扇门：接近；方法

root: approach 经古法语 aprochier 来自晚期拉丁语 appropiare「靠近」，该动词由 ad-「向」与 prope「近」构成。这个词从空间的走近出发，逐步扩展：走近一个地方的那条路就是通路与入口；面对一个问题时走的那条路就是方法；季节与截止日期也会在时间上靠近；而开始处理一件事，本质上就是先靠近它。

sensesIntro.en: Five uses radiate from nearness: walking closer, a road in, a method, the start of handling, and a season drawing near.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个用法从「近」辐射出去：走近、进去的路、方法、开始处理，以及季节临近。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: footsteps on a road, closing the distance to a door.
core.cn: 核心意象：路上的脚步，一点点缩短与一扇门的距离。

branches.en: THE DISTANCE LINE: the body moves closer.
branches.cn: 距离线：身体向目标靠近。

branches.en: THE METHOD LINE: the road becomes a way of thinking.
branches.cn: 方法线：那条路变成一种思路。

branches.en: THE HANDLING LINE: coming close is the first move.
branches.cn: 处理线：靠近就是第一个动作。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR LINE: a season closes the distance in time.
branches.cn: 日历线：季节在时间上缩短距离。

branches.en: THE ROAD LINE: the noun names the path itself.
branches.cn: 道路线：名词命名那条路本身。

intro.en: Approach is a French-shaped Latin verb, and its suffixes are all productive in English.
intro.cn: approach 是一个法语外形的拉丁动词，它的后缀在英语里都还能产词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is prope 'near', visible inside appropiare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 prope「近」，它就在 appropiare 里面。

items.example: The train approached the station slowly.

definition_zh: 合适的；恰当的；拨出（专款）；挪用；占用；专属的
definition_en: suitable for a particular situation; to set aside money for a purpose; or to take something for one's own use
core_image: 把一件东西放到它正好该在的位置上
scene: 会议室里，主管把预算表摊在桌上。The committee set aside an appropriate sum for the new library.
sceneCN: 这里 appropriate 是「合适的；恰当的」（第 1 个义项：与情境相称、适宜的）；句意为「委员会为新图书馆拨出了一笔合适的款项」。画面里有会议桌、摊开的预算表与围坐的委员。

pos.zh: 形容词：合适的；恰当的；专属的
动词：拨出；挪用；占用

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「恰当地；合适地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「恰当；得体」
由本词加 -ation 构成，义为「拨款；挪用；专款」
由 mis- 加本词构成，义为「挪用；侵吞」

senses.title: Suitable for the situation
senses.definition: suitable or right for a particular situation, purpose, or person
senses.definitionCN: 与特定情境、用途或人相称、适宜的
senses.example: The committee set aside an appropriate sum for the new library.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会为新图书馆拨出了一笔合适的款项。
senses.why: Late Latin appropriare meant to make something one's own or to fit it to its purpose; what fits its purpose is appropriate.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 appropriare 意为使某物归自己所有，或使它贴合其用途；贴合用途的就是合适的。

senses.title: To set money aside
senses.definition: to set aside money for a particular use, especially by a public body
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途留出款项，尤指公共机构这样做
senses.example: The city appropriated funds for the new bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 市里为这座新桥拨了款。
senses.why: To appropriate money is to assign it to a purpose, making that purpose its proper place.
senses.whyCN: 拨出款项就是把钱指定给一个用途，让那个用途成为它应在的位置。

senses.title: To take for one's own use
senses.definition: to take something, especially money or property, for one's own use, often wrongly
senses.definitionCN: 把某物，尤指钱财，拿来自己使用，通常指不当占有
senses.example: He was accused of appropriating the company's data.
senses.exampleCN: 他被指控挪用公司的数据。
senses.why: The same act of making something one's own turns wrong when the thing belongs to someone else.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「据为己有」的动作，当东西属于别人时就变成了错的。

senses.title: Belonging by nature
senses.definition: belonging to a particular person, group, or thing by nature
senses.definitionCN: 按本性属于特定的人、群体或事物
senses.example: Each region has its appropriate customs and songs.
senses.exampleCN: 每个地区都有它特有的习俗与歌谣。
senses.why: Proprius meant 'one's own'; what belongs to a thing by nature is appropriate to it.
senses.whyCN: proprius 意为「自己的」；按本性属于某物的东西，就是它的专属之物。

intro.en: Appropriate rests on the Latin word for 'one's own', and its senses move between fitting and taking.
intro.cn: appropriate 建立在拉丁语「自己的」一词上，词义在「相称」与「占有」之间移动。

items.en: Proprius means 'one's own, particular', and it also gives English proper and property.
items.cn: proprius 意为「自己的、特有的」，它还生出英语的 proper 与 property。

items.en: Ad- plus proprius formed appropriare, 'to make one's own, to fit to'.
items.cn: ad- 与 proprius 构成 appropriare，意为「使成为自己的、使贴合」。

items.en: French approprier passes the verb into English with both the fitting and the owning sense.
items.cn: 法语 approprier 把这个动词带进英语，相称与占有两义一同进入。

items.en: The adjective and the verb appear in the sixteenth century, close in date.
items.cn: 形容词与动词都在十六世纪出现，时间上很接近。

items.en: Public finance makes 'set aside' a major sense, while law marks out the wrongful taking.
items.cn: 公共财政使「拨出」成为主要义项，而法律则标出那种不当占有。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the proprius family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of fitness.
note.cn: 形近组收 proprius 词族的词；近义组收表示「适宜」的形容词。

entries.definition: Money set aside, or the act of taking something over.
entries.definitionCN: 由本词派生的名词，义为「拨款、专款」或「挪用、占用」。

entries.definition: To take money or property dishonestly for one's own use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挪用、侵吞」，由 mis- 加本词构成。

entries.definition: Correctness of behaviour in social situations.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「得体、礼节」，与 appropriate 同出 proprius。

entries.definition: Correct, suitable, or strictly belonging to something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「恰当的、适当的」，与本词同根。

entries.definition: Right or acceptable for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 适合某用途的，与 appropriate 的「合适」义最接近。

entries.definition: Correct according to rule or custom.
entries.definitionCN: 合乎规则或习俗的，比 appropriate 更强调规矩。

entries.definition: Right for a particular occasion or person.
entries.definitionCN: 适合某场合或某人的，语体偏文学。

entries.definition: Exactly suited to the case, often of words.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好切合情境的，常用于言辞，比 appropriate 更精准。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use proprius 'one's own' to link fitting, funding and taking.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子用 proprius「自己的」把相称、拨款与占有连起来。

normal.en: Proprius means one's own; appropriate is what belongs in its place.
normal.cn: proprius 意为自己的；appropriate 就是属于它应在位置的东西。

normal.en: A fitting thing is one that sits well in its own place.
normal.cn: 合适的东西，就是待在自己位置上很妥帖的东西。

normal.en: Money appropriated is money given its own purpose.
normal.cn: 拨出去的款项，就是被指定了专有用途的钱。

normal.en: Taking what is not yours makes the same word wrong.
normal.cn: 拿走不属于自己的东西，让同一个词变坏。

normal.en: Appropriate customs belong to a place by nature.
normal.cn: 特有的习俗，是某个地方天然自带的东西。

abstract.en: One word holds fitness, funding and theft.
abstract.cn: 一个词装着合宜、拨款与侵占。

abstract.en: All three turn on the question: whose place is this.
abstract.cn: 这三者都取决于同一个问题：这是谁的位置。

abstract.en: The word is a small study of ownership and order.
abstract.cn: 这个词是关于归属与秩序的一则小研究。

examples.cn: 委员会为新图书馆拨出了一笔合适的款项。

examples.en: The city appropriated funds for the new bridge.
examples.cn: 市里为这座新桥拨了款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普罗普里埃特」——把东西放到它自己该待的位置：合适的；拨出

root: appropriate 来自晚期拉丁语 appropriare「使成为自己的、使贴合」，该动词由 ad- 与 proprius「自己的、特有的」构成，proprius 更早的来源存疑。经法语进入英语后，这个词一边表示「贴合的、相称的」，即合适与得体；一边表示把东西归到某个用途或某个人名下：把钱归给一项公共用途就是拨出专款，把别人的东西归给自己就是挪用，而按本性归属于某物的东西则是它的专属特征。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses turn on ownership and fit: what sits right in its place, money given a purpose, something taken wrongly, and what belongs by nature.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法都围绕归属与贴合：待对位置的东西、被指定用途的钱、被错误拿走的东西，以及按本性属于某物的特征。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object placed exactly into the slot made for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西被恰好放进为它留出的位置。

branches.en: THE FIT LINE: what matches its situation is appropriate.
branches.cn: 贴合线：与情境相称的东西就是合适的。

branches.en: THE BUDGET LINE: money is given a purpose of its own.
branches.cn: 预算线：钱被指定了专有的用途。

branches.en: THE TAKING LINE: making another's thing one's own is wrong.
branches.cn: 占有线：把别人的东西变成自己的，就是错的。

branches.en: THE NATURE LINE: some things belong to a place by nature.
branches.cn: 本性线：有些东西天然属于一个地方。

branches.en: THE ORDER LINE: fit and belonging are two sides of one idea.
branches.cn: 秩序线：贴合与归属是同一个观念的两面。

intro.en: Appropriate is a Latin derivative of proprius, and the family keeps showing the root.
intro.cn: appropriate 是 proprius 的拉丁派生词，词族里不断显出这个词根。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is real: proprius 'one's own' is the source of the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是真实的：proprius「自己的」是整组词的源头。

items.meaning: suitable, or to take for a purpose
items.example: Wear appropriate shoes for the hike.
items.exampleCN: 徒步时穿合适的鞋。

items.example: She answered appropriately for the occasion.
items.exampleCN: 她的回答很合场合。

items.example: He questioned the appropriateness of the joke.
items.exampleCN: 他质疑这个笑话是否得体。

items.meaning: money set aside or a taking over
items.example: The appropriation passed the council easily.
items.exampleCN: 这笔拨款在议会顺利通过。

items.example: He misappropriated the club's funds.
items.exampleCN: 他挪用了俱乐部的资金。

items.example: They behaved with perfect propriety.
items.exampleCN: 他们举止十分得体。

items.example: Use the proper tool for the job.
items.exampleCN: 干这活要用合适的工具。

items.example: The family owns property near the river.
items.exampleCN: 这家人在河边有房产。

definition_zh: 批准；同意；赞许；认可；（商品）看货后再决定
definition_en: official permission for something, a favourable opinion, or an arrangement in which goods may be returned if unsatisfactory
core_image: 一枚印章落在纸面，事情从此被允许
scene: 办公桌上摊着一份方案，签字笔停在纸边。The plan cannot start until it receives official approval.
sceneCN: 这里 approval 是「批准；同意」（第 1 个义项：官方对某事的许可）；句意为「方案必须得到正式批准才能启动」。画面里有办公桌、摊开的方案与停在纸边的签字笔。

pos.zh: 名词：批准；同意；赞许；认可

collocations.zh: 看货后再决定（不合可退）

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀 -al 得到的动词，义为「批准；赞成」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「赞许的」
由 approving 加 -ly 构成，义为「赞许地」
由 dis- 加 approve 构成，义为「不赞成」

senses.title: Official permission
senses.definition: official permission or agreement for a plan, request, or action
senses.definitionCN: 官方对计划、请求或行动给予的许可或同意
senses.example: The plan cannot start until it receives official approval.
senses.exampleCN: 方案必须得到正式批准才能启动。
senses.why: Approve comes from Latin approbare, 'to mark as good'; approval is the state of having been marked good.
senses.whyCN: approve 来自拉丁语 approbare「打上好之印记」；approval 就是被盖上认可之印的状态。

senses.title: A favourable opinion
senses.definition: a favourable opinion of someone or something, often shown rather than spoken
senses.definitionCN: 对某人某物的赞同看法，常以神态而非言语表现
senses.example: She smiled at him with quiet approval.
senses.exampleCN: 她朝他微笑，带着无声的赞许。
senses.why: The same stamp can be given by a look rather than by a pen.
senses.whyCN: 同一枚印章，也可以由一个眼神而不是笔来盖下。

senses.title: Goods taken on trial
senses.definition: in the phrase on approval, an arrangement in which goods are supplied and may be returned if not satisfactory
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 on approval，指先取货、不满意可退的安排
senses.example: He took the coat home on approval.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那件外套拿回家，看过再决定买不买。
senses.why: The buyer is given time to judge the goods, and only then is the stamp given.
senses.whyCN: 买方先被给了判断货物的时间，到那时才盖上那枚印章。

senses.title: The level of public support
senses.definition: the level of public support shown in polls, as in an approval rating
senses.definitionCN: 民意调查中显示的公众支持程度，如支持率
senses.example: The mayor's approval rating fell after the strike.
senses.exampleCN: 罢工之后，市长的支持率下降了。
senses.why: Opinion polls turn scattered nods into a number, measuring how much stamping the public is willing to do.
senses.whyCN: 民意调查把零散的点头变成一个数字，衡量公众愿意盖多少认可之印。

intro.en: Approval is approve plus the noun suffix -al, and the Latin idea is a mark that says good.
intro.cn: approval 是 approve 加名词后缀 -al，拉丁观念里那是一个写着「好」的记号。

items.en: Probus means 'good, upright', and it stands behind the verb of testing and approving.
items.cn: probus 意为「好的、正直的」，它是检验与认可那个动词背后的形容词。

items.en: Probare 'to test, prove' first meant to make or show something good.
items.cn: probare「检验、证明」最初意为使某物变好，或显示出它是好的。

items.en: Ad- plus probare gave approbare, 'to assent to, to approve'.
items.cn: ad- 与 probare 构成 approbare，意为「同意、认可」。

entries.definition: Public support for a person, plan, or product.

entries.definition: Words expressing warm approval.
entries.definitionCN: 表达热烈赞许的话，情感比 approval 更外露。

normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子都把印章、点头或民调看成同一枚「好」的记号。

normal.en: Approve plus -al: the state of being marked good.
normal.cn: approve 加 -al：被盖上好之印记的状态。

normal.en: An official stamp says the plan may begin.
normal.cn: 一枚公章的印记说：方案可以开始了。

normal.en: A quiet smile can give approval without words.
normal.cn: 一个安静的微笑，可以不用说话就表示赞许。

normal.en: Goods on approval are worn before the stamp.
normal.cn: 看货再决定的商品，是先穿戴、后盖印。

normal.en: An approval rating turns nods into numbers.

abstract.en: Permission, praise and popularity are all versions of one mark.
abstract.cn: 许可、赞许与人气，都是同一枚印记的变体。

abstract.en: The word shows how a judgement becomes a document.
abstract.cn: 这个词展示了判断如何变成一纸文书。

abstract.en: To approve is always to say that something is good enough.
abstract.cn: 批准，始终是在说某物足够好。

examples.en: The plan cannot start until it receives official approval.
examples.cn: 方案必须得到正式批准才能启动。

examples.en: She smiled at him with quiet approval.
examples.cn: 她朝他微笑，带着无声的赞许。

examples.en: He took the coat home on approval.
examples.cn: 他把那件外套拿回家，看过再决定买不买。

root: approval 由 approve 加名词后缀 -al 构成。approve 来自拉丁语 approbare「同意、认可」，其形容词 probus 意为「好的、正直的」，动词 probare 则是检验并显示其好。因此 approval 的核心意象始终是「给某物盖上好之印记」：官方盖印就是批准，一个眼神盖印就是赞许，商品先拿回家再盖印就是看货后决定，而民意调查则把这枚印记换算成支持率。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses all give the mark of good: an official stamp, a friendly look, goods kept on trial, and a poll number.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法都在盖上「好」的印记：官方批文、友善的目光、试用后再买的商品，以及民调数字。

branches.cn: 目光线：一个微笑不用笔就盖了印。

branches.en: THE TRIAL LINE: the buyer judges before the stamp is given.
branches.cn: 试用线：买方先判断，之后才盖印。

branches.en: THE POLL LINE: scattered nods are counted as a number.
branches.cn: 民调线：零散的点头被计成一个数字。

branches.en: THE TRUST LINE: official and personal approval both build confidence.
branches.cn: 信任线：官方与私人的认可都在建立信心。

items.exampleCN: 这些书是看货后再决定是否购买的。

definition_en: to officially agree to or permit something, or to think that someone or something is good

senses.title: To give official permission
senses.definition: to officially agree to or permit a plan, request, or action
senses.definitionCN: 正式同意或允许某项计划、请求或行动
senses.example: The committee voted to approve the new course in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会投票通过了春季的新课程。
senses.why: Latin approbare was to give something the mark of good, and a committee does exactly that with a proposal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 approbare 是给某物打上「好」的记号，委员会对提案所做的正是这件事。

senses.title: To think well of something
senses.definition: to consider someone or something good, right, or acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 认为某人某物是好的、正确的或可接受的

senses.exampleCN: 她的父母不赞成她熬夜。

senses.title: To judge someone fit

senses.title: To permit official use

senses.exampleCN: 这种药去年获批用于儿童。
senses.why: Official bodies stamp products as good before the public may use them.
senses.whyCN: 官方机构先给产品盖上「好」的印记，公众才能使用。

intro.en: Approve is a Latin verb of testing and marking good, brought to English through French.
intro.cn: approve 是一个表示检验并打上「好」记号的拉丁动词，经法语传入英语。

items.en: Probus means 'good, upright', the adjective behind the testing verb.
items.cn: probus 意为「好的、正直的」，是那个检验动词背后的形容词。

items.en: Probare 'to test, prove' first meant to make or show something good.
items.cn: probare「检验、证明」最初意为使某物变好，或显示出它是好的。

items.en: Approbare 'to assent to' adds ad- to probare and gives the word its approving force.
items.cn: approbare「同意」在 probare 前加 ad-，赋予这个词认可的力量。

items.en: French aprover brings the verb to English, where it is recorded in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 aprover 把这个动词带到英语，十四世纪已有记录。

items.en: The word now covers official permission and personal opinion alike.
items.cn: 这个词现在同时覆盖官方许可与个人意见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the approve family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of authorizing and accepting.
note.cn: 形近组收 approve 的词族；近义组收表示授权与接受的动词。

definition_zh: 大约的；近似的；接近；近似；估算
definition_en: close to a particular number or state but not exact; to come close to a value, or to estimate something roughly
core_image: 两支箭落在靶心附近，却没有一支正中
scene: 地图铺在桌上，铅笔在两点之间画了一条线。The distance is approximate because the road curves.
sceneCN: 这里 approximate 是「大约的；近似的」（第 1 个义项：接近某一数值但不精确）；句意为「这个距离只是近似的，因为道路是弯的」。画面里有摊开的地图、两点之间的铅笔线与一把量尺。

pos.zh: 形容词：大约的；近似的；大致相似的
动词：接近；近似；估算

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「大约；近似地」

senses.title: Close but not exact
senses.definition: close to a particular number, amount, or description but not exactly correct
senses.definitionCN: 接近某个数值、数量或描述，但不完全精确
senses.example: The distance is approximate because the road curves.
senses.exampleCN: 这个距离只是近似的，因为道路是弯的。
senses.why: Late Latin approximare meant to come very near; the adjective describes what stands near the true value without touching it.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 approximare 意为靠得很近；形容词描述的是贴近真值却没有碰上的东西。

senses.title: To come close to a value
senses.definition: to come close to a particular value, standard, or quality
senses.definitionCN: 接近某个数值、标准或品质
senses.example: His account approximates the truth without being exact.
senses.exampleCN: 他的叙述接近真相，但并不完全准确。
senses.why: The verb keeps the movement: getting nearer to a target.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了那个动作：向目标靠近。

senses.title: To estimate roughly
senses.definition: to calculate or estimate something roughly rather than exactly
senses.definitionCN: 对某物作粗略而非精确的计算或估计
senses.example: We approximated the cost at two thousand pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 我们估算费用约为两千英镑。
senses.why: An estimate is a number placed near the true figure, as near as one can get.
senses.whyCN: 估算是把一个数字放在真值附近，能靠多近就靠多近。

senses.title: To resemble closely
senses.definition: to resemble something closely in appearance or character
senses.definitionCN: 在外观或特征上与被比较之物很接近
senses.example: The copy approximates the original very well.
senses.exampleCN: 这件仿品与原件非常接近。
senses.why: Two things can stand near each other without being the same.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西可以彼此靠得很近，却并不相同。

intro.en: Approximate is built on the Latin word for nearest, and it names what stands close to the truth.
intro.cn: approximate 建立在拉丁语「最近的」一词上，命名的是贴近真相的东西。

items.en: Prope 'near' is the adverb behind the whole family of closeness.
items.cn: prope「近」是整族表示接近的词背后的副词。

items.en: Proximus is the superlative, 'nearest', and it also gives English proximity.
items.cn: proximus 是最高级「最近的」，它还生出英语的 proximity。

items.en: Ad- plus proximus formed approximare, 'to come near to'.
items.cn: ad- 与 proximus 构成 approximare，意为「靠近」。

items.en: The adjective and verb appear in English in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.
items.cn: 形容词与动词在十五、十六世纪先后出现在英语里。

items.en: The word covers rough figures, close copies and near matches of every kind.
items.cn: 这个词覆盖粗略数字、接近的仿品与各种近似匹配。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the proximity family; the near-meaning group gathers words for rough and close.
note.cn: 形近组收表示「邻近」的词族；近义组收表示粗略与接近的词。

entries.definition: Nearest in space, time, or cause.

entries.definition: The state of being near.

entries.definition: Not exact, made without careful measurement.

entries.definition: Near in space, value, or similarity.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普罗克西梅特」——箭落在靶心旁边，差一点点：大约的；近似

root: approximate 来自晚期拉丁语 approximare「靠近」，该动词由 ad- 与 proximus「最近的」构成，proximus 又是 prope「近」的最高级。这个词的核心始终是「贴近而未必正中」：一个数字贴近真值就是近似值，一份叙述贴近真相就是接近，一笔费用靠估算贴近实际就是估算，一件仿品贴近原件就是大致相似。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses all stand near a target without hitting it: a rough figure, a close account, an estimate, and a good copy.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法都站在目标附近而没有正中：粗略的数字、接近的叙述、估算，以及逼真的仿品。

branches.en: THE VALUE LINE: the number stands near the true one.

branches.cn: 动作线：动词向目标移动。

branches.en: THE ESTIMATE LINE: a rough figure is placed near the truth.
branches.cn: 估算线：粗略的数字被放在真相附近。

branches.en: THE COPY LINE: a likeness stands close to its original.
branches.cn: 仿品线：相似之物站在原件附近。

branches.en: THE MEASURE LINE: both adjective and estimate accept a small gap.
branches.cn: 度量线：形容词与估算都容许一点差距。

intro.en: Approximate is a Latin verb and adjective built on proximus, and its family is easy to read.

definition_zh: 建筑师；缔造者；设计者；架构师
definition_en: a person who designs buildings, or someone who creates and guides a large plan, idea, or system
core_image: 在蓝图上勾出一条屋脊线，让想法有了骨架
scene: 绘图桌前，一支铅笔在蓝图上勾出屋脊线。The architect sketched the outline of the museum on tracing paper.

pos.zh: 名词：建筑师；缔造者；设计者；架构师

senses.title: A designer of buildings
senses.definition: a person trained to design buildings and supervise their construction
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、负责设计建筑并监督施工的人
senses.example: The architect sketched the outline of the museum on tracing paper.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师在描图纸上勾出博物馆的轮廓。
senses.why: Greek arkhitekton joined 'chief' and 'builder': the architect is the one who directs the building.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 arkhitekton 把「首要的」与「建造者」连在一起：建筑师就是指挥建造的人。

senses.title: The creator of a large undertaking
senses.definition: a person who plans and guides a large undertaking, such as a reform or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 筹划并引导一项大型事业的人，如改革或机构
senses.example: He was the architect of the peace agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 他是这份和平协议的缔造者。
senses.why: The image of a building spreads to any large structure: a treaty also needs a plan and a builder.
senses.whyCN: 建筑的意象扩散到任何大型结构：一份条约同样需要图纸与建造者。

senses.title: A designer of systems
senses.definition: a person who designs the structure of a computer system or a large organization
senses.definitionCN: 设计计算机系统或大型组织整体结构的人
senses.example: She works as a systems architect for the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 她在银行担任系统架构师。
senses.why: A system has parts that must bear weight and fit together, just as a building does.
senses.whyCN: 系统也有必须承重并彼此吻合的部件，正如一栋建筑。

senses.title: The first planner of an idea
senses.definition: the original creator of a method, idea, or style
senses.definitionCN: 某种方法、思想或风格的最初创造者
senses.example: He is remembered as the architect of modern ecology.
senses.exampleCN: 他被人们记作现代生态学的开创者。
senses.why: Whoever draws the first plan of a new field is its architect.
senses.whyCN: 谁为一个新领域画出第一张图，谁就是它的缔造者。

intro.en: Architect is a Greek word carried into English through Latin and French, and it still means chief builder.
intro.cn: architect 是一个经拉丁语与法语传入英语的希腊词，意思仍是「首要的建造者」。

items.en: Tekton means 'builder, craftsman', the everyday word for a worker in wood or stone.
items.cn: tekton 意为「建造者、匠人」，是木石工匠的日常称呼。

items.en: Arkhi- 'chief' plus tekton gave arkhitekton, 'chief builder, master builder'.
items.cn: arkhi-「首要的」与 tekton 构成 arkhitekton，意为「总建造师、匠师」。

items.en: Latin borrows the Greek word as architectus, keeping the sense of a master designer.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊词借作 architectus，保留「设计主事者」的意思。

items.en: French architecte passes the word into English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 architecte 在十六世纪把这个词送入英语。

items.en: The word extends from buildings to treaties, organizations and computer systems.
items.cn: 这个词从建筑扩展到条约、组织与计算机系统。

senses.title: The art of designing buildings
senses.definition: the art, science, and study of designing buildings and other structures
senses.definitionCN: 设计建筑及其他构筑物的艺术、科学与学问
senses.example: He went to Rome to study architecture.
senses.exampleCN: 他去罗马学习建筑学。
senses.why: Greek arkhitekton named the master builder; the abstract noun names the knowledge and craft that make him one.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 arkhitekton 命名总建造师；这个抽象名词命名的是使他成为总建造师的知识与手艺。

senses.title: The style of buildings
senses.definition: the style in which buildings are designed, especially that of a period or place
senses.definitionCN: 建筑设计所呈现的式样，尤指某一时期或地方特有的式样
senses.example: She studied the architecture of the old town for her thesis.
senses.exampleCN: 她为写论文研究了这座老城的建筑。
senses.why: What the craft produces can be seen in stone: the style of a town is its architecture made visible.
senses.whyCN: 手艺的产物能在石头里被看见：一座城的风格就是变得可见的建筑学。

senses.title: The structure of a system
senses.definition: the overall structure and organization of a computer system, organization, or other complex thing
senses.definitionCN: 计算机系统、组织或其他复杂事物的整体结构与编排方式
senses.example: The architecture of the network must be redrawn.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网络的体系结构必须重新绘制。
senses.why: Any complex thing has load-bearing parts and a plan, so the building word moves to systems.
senses.whyCN: 任何复杂事物都有承重部件与一张图，于是建筑词转向系统。

senses.title: Buildings taken as a body of work
senses.definition: buildings and other structures considered together, especially those of a place or period
senses.definitionCN: 被整体看待的建筑物，尤指某地或某时期的建筑
senses.example: The city's architecture mixes glass towers and stone courts.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的建筑混合了玻璃高塔与石砌庭院。
senses.why: The built things are still called by the name of the art that made them.
senses.whyCN: 被建造出来的众多事物，仍用造就它们的这门艺术之名来称呼。
